description.p: TECHNICAL FILED
[0001] The present invention relates to a plasma guide wire.
BACKGROUND ART

[0002] Conventionally, plasma guide wires are known. For example, Patent Document 1 discloses a plasma guide wire 100 as shown in Fig. 6 including a guide wire body 120 and an insulating resin tube 130 covering the guide wire body 120. In the guide wire body 120, a coil 124 is wound around on the outer periphery of a region at the front end side of a core shaft 122, and a tip 126 is joined to the front end of the core shaft 122 and the front end of the coil 124. The rear end of the coil 124 is joined to the core shaft 122 at a coil-core shaft joining region 125. The insulating resin tube 130 includes a first insulating resin tube 131 and a second insulating resin tube 132. The first insulating resin tube 131 is disposed on the outer periphery of the coil 124, and extends from the tip 126 to the rearward of the coil-core shaft joining region 125. The second insulating resin tube 132 is disposed on the outer periphery of the core shaft 122, and joined to the rear end of the first insulating resin tube 131, and extends from the rear end of the first insulating resin tube 131 to the rearward of the core shaft 122. The plasma guide wire 100 as described above may be used to generate plasma between the front end of the tip 126 and an electrode of a separate member facing that front end when a high-frequency generator is connected to the rear end of the core shaft 122. This enables plasma to perforate an occluded portion of a blood vessel.

DISCLOSURE OF THE INVENTION
Problems to be Solved by the Invention

[0004] Nonetheless, a configuration where the first insulating resin tube 131 and the second insulating resin tube 132 are composed of different materials is not mentioned in any way in Patent Document 1. Consequently, the operativity of a portion of the guide wire body 120 where the coil 124 is wound around may be decreased if the first insulating resin tube 131 and the second insulating resin tube 132 are composed of the same relatively hard resin. On the other hand, a stiffness gap may be created at a portion of the first insulating resin tube 131 where the coil 124 is not present if the second insulating resin tube 132 is configured to be softer than the first insulating resin tubes 131. This may result in the following problem: the first insulating resin tube 131, which is soft, may be bend at this portion when the plasma guide wire 100 is pushed to the front-end direction. This, in turn, will decrease operativity.

[0005] The present invention is made to order to solve the problem as described above. A main object of the present invention is to improve operativity of a front end side (that is, a portion of a core shaft where a coil is wound around or/and a portion of a first insulating resin tube where a coil is not present) of a plasma guide wire.
Means for Solving the Problems
[0006] A plasma guide wire according to an aspect of the present invention includes:
a core shaft,
a coil wound around on an outer periphery of a region of a front end side of the core shaft,
a tip joined to a front end of the core shaft and a front end of the coil,
a coil-core shaft joining region joining a rear end of the coil with the core shaft,
a first insulating resin tube disposed on an outer periphery of the coil and extending from the tip to a rearward of the coil-core shaft joining region,

a second insulating resin tube disposed on an outer periphery of the core shaft, and joined to a rear end of the first insulating resin tube, and extending from the rear end of the first insulating resin tube to a rearward of the core shaft, the second insulating resin tube being harder than the first insulating resin tube, and

a third insulating resin tube disposed on at least a portion of a region of an inner periphery of the first insulating resin tube, the region being located rearwardly relative to a position facing the rear end of the coil.

[0007] According to the above plasma guide wire, a stiffness gap created at a portion of the relatively soft first insulating resin tube where the coil is not present can be reduced by virtue of the presence of the third insulating resin tube. This can prevent bending at this portion. Further, the third insulating resin tube is not disposed at a portion of the relatively soft first insulating resin tube where the relatively soft first insulating resin tube covers the coil. This can improve the operativity of the front end side of the plasma guide wire, i.e., a portion of the core shaft where the coil is wound around and/or a portion of the first insulating resin tube where the coil is not present.

PREFERRED MODE FOR CARRYING OUT THE INVENTION

[0009] Below, the suitable embodiments of the present invention will be described with reference to the figures. Fig. 1 shows a front elevational view of a plasma guide wire 10, and Fig. 2 shows a cross-sectional view along A-A of Fig. 1 , and Fig. 3 shows an enlarged view of the portion B of Fig. 2 .

[0010] As shown in Fig. 1 , the plasma guide wire 10 according to the present embodiment includes a guide wire body 20 and an insulating resin tube 30 covering the guide wire body 20. The plasma guide wire 10 has a total length of, for example, 1,800 to 2,000 mm. The plasma guide wire 10 may also be referred to as a high-frequency (RF) guide wire.
[0011] As shown in Fig. 2 , the guide wire body 20 includes a core shaft 22, a coil 24, a coil-core shaft joining region 25, and a tip 26.

[0012] The core shaft 22 is composed of an electrically conductive material, and includes a shaft rear-end portion 22a and a shaft front-end portion 22b. The shaft front-end portion 22b has alternately disposed tubular and tapered portions, and a tubular portion arranged closer to the front end has a smaller diameter. The core shaft 22 is composed of a material such as, for example, stainless steel (austenite-based stainless steel, martensite-based stainless steel, ferrite-based stainless steel, austenite-ferrite duplex stainless steel, precipitation-hardening stainless steel, and the like), a superelastic alloy (a Ni-Ti alloy and the like), a piano wire, and tungsten.

[0013] The coil 24 includes a single element wire spirally wound around on the outer periphery of a region at the front end side of the core shaft 22. The coil 24 may serve to confer flexibility on the plasma guide wire 10. An electric current from a high frequency generator 40 will flow thorough the core shaft 22 to reach the coil core shaft joining region 25, and then will branch and flow to the core shaft 22 and the coil 24. Therefore, the electric current flowing through the coil 24 is smaller than that flowing from the rear end of the core shaft 22 to the coil-core shaft joining region 25. The total length of the coil 24 is, for example, 40 mm to 50 mm, and the outer diameter of the coil 24 is, for example, 0.24 mm to 0.25 mm, and the diameter of the element wire is, for example, 0.03 to 0.08 mm. The element wire is composed of a material such as, for example, stainless steel (austenite-based stainless steel, martensite-based stainless steel, ferrite-based stainless steel, austenite-ferrite duplex stainless steel, precipitation-hardening stainless steel, and the like), a superelastic alloy (a Ni-Ti alloy and the like), and a radiopacity metal (platinum, gold, tungsten, and the like). It is noted that the coil 24 may be formed by spirally winding a plurality of element wires. Further, the coil 24 may be formed by spirally winding a stranded wire having a plurality of element wires twisted.

[0014] The coil-core shaft joining region 25 joins the rear end of the coil 24 with the core shaft 22, and is composed of a solder material. Solder materials include, for example, aluminum-alloy solder, silver solder, gold solder, zinc, Sn-Pb alloys, Pb-Ag alloys, Sn-Ag alloys, and the like. It is noted that the coil 24 may also be joined to the core shaft 22 through a solder material at the front end of the coil 24 and/or the middle portion of the coil 24 in addition to at the rear end of the coil 24.

[0015] The tip 26 is a member having a curved surface and formed by welding the front end of the core shaft 22 and the front end of the coil 24. For welding, arc welding is preferred. Further, arc welding may be of non-consumable electrode types such as TIG welding and plasma welding, or may be of consumable electrode types such as coated arc welding, MAG welding, CO<2> gas arc welding, argon-CO<2> gas arc welding, MIG welding, and submerged arc welding. Non-consumable electrode types are, however, preferred, and TIG welding is more preferred.
[0016] As shown in Fig. 2 , the insulating resin tube 30 includes a first insulating resin tube 31, a second insulating resin tube 32, and a third insulating resin tube 33.

[0017] The first insulating resin tube 31 is disposed on the outer periphery of the coil 24, and extends from the tip 26 to the rearward of the coil-core shaft joining region 25. The front end of the first insulating resin tube 31 is joined to the tip 26. The first insulating resin tube 31 is composed of, for example, a fluorine-based resin (PFA). The total length of the first insulating resin tube 31 is, for example, 100 mm to 115 mm, and the outer diameter of the first insulating resin tube 31 is, for example, 0.3 mm to 0.35 mm, and the thickness of the first insulating resin tube 31 is, for example, 0.015 mm to 0.02 mm.

[0018] The second insulating resin tube 32 is disposed on the outer periphery of the core shaft 22, and extends from the rear end of the first insulating resin tube 31 to the rearward of the core shaft 22. The second insulating resin tube 32 is bonded with the first insulating resin tube 31 through a joining region 34. The joining region 34 is formed by bonding the inner surface of the second insulating resin tube 32 at the front end with the outer surface of the first insulating resin tube 31 at the rear end via an adhesive. Adhesives include, for example, epoxy resin, acrylic resin, and the like. The second insulating resin tube 32 is composed of, for example, polyimide resin. The total length of the second insulating resin tube 32 is, for example, 1800 mm to 1900 mm, and the outer diameter of the second insulating resin tube 32 is, for example, 0.32 mm to 0.36 mm, and the thickness of the second insulating resin tube 32 is, for example, 0.005 mm to 0.015 mm. The second insulating resin tube 32 is harder than the first insulating resin tube 31. It is noted that the joining region 34 may be bonded with the core shaft 22 via an adhesive.

[0019] The third insulating resin tube 33 is arranged inside the first insulating resin tube 31. The front end of the third insulating resin tube 33 comes into contact with the coil-core shaft joining region 25. As shown in Fig. 3 , the third insulating resin tube 33 is disposed so as to cover throughout a region X of the inner periphery of the first insulating resin tube 31, the region X being located rearwardly relative to a position P facing the rear end of the coil 24. The third insulating resin tube 33 further extends to the rearward of the rear end of the first insulating resin tube 31, and covers, from the inside, the joining region 34 between the first insulating resin tube 31 between the second insulating resin tube 32. The third insulating resin tube 33 can serve to prevent the first insulating resin tube 31 from making contact with the core shaft 22. The third insulating resin tube 33 is composed of, for example, polyimide resin. The total length of the third insulating resin tube 33 is, for example, 60 mm to 80 mm, and the outer diameter of the third insulating resin tube 33 is, for example, 0.23 mm to 0.24 mm, and the thickness of the third insulating resin tube 33 is, for example, 0.015 mm to 0.02 mm. The third insulating resin tube 33 is harder than the first insulating resin tube 31. The third insulating resin tube 33 may have a front end and a rear end bonded with the core shaft 22 via an adhesive.

[0020] Next, an exemplary use of the plasma guide wire 10. The plasma guide wire 10, which can serve as a medical mechanical device for use in percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PCI), may be used for guiding a device such as a balloon and a stent to an occluded portion of a blood vessel. In the plasma guide wire 10, the front end portion of the core shaft 22 corresponds to the distal portion, and the rear end portion of the core shaft 22 corresponds to the proximal portion. The distal portion of the plasma guide wire 10 is inserted into a blood vessel, and the proximal portion is operated by an operator such as a physician. Once the distal portion reaches an occluded portion in a blood vessel, an operator pushes, pulls, and/or rotates the plasma guide wire 10 so that the tip 26 may penetrate the occluded portion. However, these operations alone may not be sufficient enough to penetrate the occluded portion if the occluded portion is hardened due to calcification. If that is the case, a separate plasma guide wire 10 may be introduced into the blood vessel from the opposite side to place the tip 26 of the separate plasma guide wire 10 in the side opposite to the occluded portion. This leads to a state where a pair of the tips 26 are arranged to be opposed to each other across the occluded portion. High-frequency voltage is then applied between the pair of tips 26 to generate plasma between the pair of tips 26, thereby destroying the occluded portion.

[0021] Here, a stiffness gap may be created in the plasma guide wire 10 at a portion of the relatively soft first insulating resin tubes 31 where the coil 24 is not present, but the stiffness gap can be reduced by virtue of the presence of the third insulating resin tube 33. This can prevent bending at this portion. Further, the third insulating resin tube 33 is not disposed on a portion of the relatively soft first insulating resin tubes 31 where the relatively soft first insulating resin tubes 31 covers the coil 24. This can improve the operativity of the front end side of the plasma guide wire 10, i.e., a portion of the core shaft 22 where the coil 24 is wound around.

[0022] In the plasma guide wire 10 according to the present embodiment as described above, the operativity of the front end side of the plasma guide wire 10 can be improved (i.e., a portion of the core shafts 22 where the coil 24 is wound around or/and a portion of the first insulating resin tube where the coil is not present).

[0023] Further, a softer resin generally tends to have lower thermal resistance while a harder resin tends to have higher thermal resistance. The first insulating resin tube 31, which is relatively soft and thus has low thermal resistance, may not be able to maintain insulation when making direct contact with the core shaft 22 which is heated to high temperature due to the flow of high-frequency current. However, the third insulating resin tube 33 can serve to prevent the first insulating resin tube 31 from making contact with the core shaft 22. Therefore, insulation of the first insulating resin tube 31 can be better ensured. It is noted that the first insulating resin tube 31 may actually make contact with the coil 24, but the coil 24 is unlikely to be heated to such high temperature. Therefore, insulation will not be compromised. This is because an electric current flowing through the coil 24 upon plasma generation is smaller than that flowing from the rear end of the core shaft 22 through the coil-core shaft joining region 25.

[0024] Further, the third insulating resin tube 33, which is harder than the first insulating resin tube 31, can further reduce the stiffness gap created at a portion of the first insulating resin tubes 31 where the coil 24 is not present.

[0025] Still further, the third insulating resin tube 33, which is disposed so as to cover, from the inside, the joining region 34 between the first insulating resin tube 31 and the second insulating resin tube 32, can better ensure insulation at the joining region.

[0026] Yet further, the third insulating resin tube 33, which comes into contact with the coil-core shaft joining region 25 under a large electric load due to the confluence of an electric current flowing through the coil 24 and an electric current flowing through the core shaft 22, can better ensure insulation at the coil-core shaft joining region 25.

[0027] Even further, the third insulating resin tube 33, which is disposed throughout at the region X of the inner periphery of the first insulating resin tube 31, the region X being located rearwardly relative to the position P facing the rear end of the coil 24, can further reduce the stiffness gap created at a portion of the first insulating resin tube 31 where the coil 24 is not present, and can also better ensure insulation of the first insulating resin tube 31.

[0028] It is noted that the present invention shall not be limited to the aforementioned embodiments, and the present invention can be implemented according to various aspects as long as they fall within the technical scope of the present invention.

[0029] According to the aforementioned embodiments, the third insulating resin tube 33 is disposed throughout at the region X of the inner periphery of the first insulating resin tube 31, the region X being located rearwardly relative to the position P facing the rear end of the coil 24. However, the third insulating resin tube 33 may be disposed at a portion of the region X. For example, the third insulating resin tube 33 may be divided into third insulating resin tubes 35, 36, 37 as shown in Fig. 4 . It is noted that in Fig. 4 , the same reference symbols are given to the same components as the aforementioned embodiments. Even in the case of this configuration, the stiffness gap at a portion of the first insulating resin tubes 31 where the coil 24 is not present can be reduced by virtue of the presence of the third insulating resin tubes 35, 36, 37. This can prevent bending at this portion. Further, the third insulating resin tubes 35, 36, 37 are not disposed on a portion of the first insulating resin tubes 31 where the first insulating resin tubes 31 covers the coil 24. This can improve the operativity of the front end side of the plasma guide wire 10, i.e., a portion of the core shaft 22 where the coil 24 is wound around. It is not noted that the third insulating resin tubes 35, 36, 37 are preferably disposed so as to prevent the first insulating resin tube 31 from making contact with the core shaft 22. Further, any one or two of the third insulating resin tubes 35, 36, 37 may be used. When the third insulating resin tube 35 is used, insulation at the coil-core shaft joining region 25 can be better ensured. When the third insulating resin tube 37 is used, insulation at the joining region 34 can be better ensured.

[0030] In the aforementioned embodiments, the tip 26 of the plasma guide wire 10 and the tip 26 of the separate plasma guide wire 10 are arranged to be opposed to each other across an occluded portion inside a blood vessel, and then plasma is generated between the pair of the tips 26 while that state is maintained. However, plasma may be generated by another way. For example, plasma may be generated between the tip 26 of the plasma guide wire 10 inserted into a patient's blood vessel and an electrode arranged on the patient's skin. Alternatively, two of the plasma guide wires 10 are delivered through a blood vessel in a parallel fashion, and plasma may be generated between the tips 26 of them near an occluded portion to destroy the occluded portion.

[0031] In the aforementioned embodiments, a collar 38 having a ring-like shape and composed of a heat resistant resin (for example, polyimide resin and others) may be disposed at the front end of the first insulating resin tube 31, and the collar 38 may be joined to the tip 26 as shown in Fig. 5 . It is noted that in Fig. 5 , the same reference symbols are given to the same components as the aforementioned embodiments. This configuration can prevent heat damage of the front end of the first insulating resin tube 31.

[0032] In the aforementioned embodiments, the second insulating resin tube 32 may extend to the end face of the shaft rear-end portion 22a. Alternatively, a portion of the shaft rear-end portion 22a of the core shaft 22, the portion being not coated with the second insulating resin tube 32, may be coated with another insulating resin tube (a fourth insulating resin tube).

[0033] In the aforementioned embodiments, one harder than the first insulating resin tube 31 is used as the third insulating resin tube 33. However, the configuration shall not be limited to this. For example, one having the same hardness as the first insulating resin tube 31 may be used as the third insulating resin tube 33, or one softer than the first insulating resin tube 31 may be used. Even if these configurations are used, the stiffness gap at a portion of the first insulating resin tubes 31 where the coil 24 is not present can be reduced, leading to improved operativity of the front end side of the plasma guide wire 10. However, one harder than the first insulating resin tube 31 is preferably used as the third insulating resin tube 33 because the stiffness gap can be further reduced.

[0034] In the aforementioned embodiments, a material harder than that of the first insulating resin tube 31 is used for the third insulating resin tube 33. However, the material shall not be limited to this. For example, one made of the same material as first insulating resin tube 31 but thicker than the first insulating resin tube 31 may be used as the third insulating resin tube 33. Even if this configuration is used, the third insulating resin tube 33 can be made harder than the first insulating resin tube 31. It is noted that the hardness for the materials of the first insulating resin tube 31, the second insulating resin tube 32, and the third insulating resin tube 33 means the hardness in terms of Shore hardness or the hardness in terms of durometer hardness. Therefore, the hardness for these materials can be measured using a known testing machine.
[0035] It is noted that the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention can also be configured, without limitation but for example, as follows.

[0036] In the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention, the third insulating resin tube may be disposed so as to prevent the first insulating resin tube from making contact with the core shaft. In general, a softer resin tends to have lower thermal resistance while a harder resin tends to have higher thermal resistance. The first insulating resin tube, which is relatively soft and thus has low thermal resistance, may not be able to maintain insulation when making direct contact with the core shaft which is heated to high temperature due to the flow of high-frequency current. Here, the third insulating resin tube is disposed so as to prevent the first insulating resin tube from making contact with the core shaft, leading to better ensured insulation of the first insulating resin tube.

[0037] In the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention, the third insulating resin tube may be harder than the first insulating resin tube. This can further reduce the stiffness gap created at a portion of the first insulating resin tube where the coil is not present.

[0038] In the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention, the third insulating resin tube may be disposed so as to cover a joining position between the first insulating resin tube and the second insulating resin tube. This can better ensure insulation at the joining position between the first insulating resin tube and the second insulating resin tube.

[0039] In the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention, the third insulating resin tube may come into contact with the coil-core shaft joining region. This configuration where the third insulating resin tube comes into contact with the coil-core shaft joining region under a large electric load due to the confluence of an electric current flowing through the coil and an electric current flowing through the core shaft, can better ensure insulation at the coil-core shaft joining region.

[0040] In the plasma guide wire according to an embodiment of the present invention, the third insulating resin tube may be disposed throughout at a region of the inner periphery of the first insulating resin tube, the region being located rearwardly relative to a position facing the rear end of the coil. This can further reduce the stiffness gap created at a portion of the first insulating resin tube where the coil is not present, and can also better ensure insulation of the first insulating resin tube.
Industrial applicability
[0041] The present invention can be implemented as a medical mechanical device for use in, for example, percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PCI).
